markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (84%)** · Ambiguous: Benign vs InSitu · Careful review

Invasive probability is low (3%), but Benign stays in the 90% conformal set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 84%, Benign 13% | Clear leader, Benign second |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu | Two classes unresolved |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.955 / 94th percentile | No input flag raised |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 5/5 InSitu | Neighbors support suggestion |

## Tissue evidence
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 8, 11) · ↓ invasive · Prominent; associated with lower invasive likelihood · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 0, 1, 6) · ↓ invasive · Prominent; also associated with lower invasive likelihood · Weak
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (region 6) · ↓ invasive · Low score; associated with lower invasive likelihood; spot check 0/20 · Unreliable
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 2) · ↓ invasive · Score near typical; strongest in region 2 only · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions cuts the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47 to 0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect versus random is 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007), so unproven; mitoses (0/20 spot check) is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Benign and InSitu cannot be separated; the conformal set holds both.
- Region 2 (84% regional invasive risk) reflects true invasion that the whole-image 3% understates.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 0, 1, 6**: gland architecture; decide benign atypia versus duct-confined in situ.
2. **Region 2**: highest regional invasive contribution (84% risk); look for stromal invasion.
3. **Regions 2, 3, 7, 10, 11**: margin segments scored tumor [F7]; confirm tumor at edge.
